nodes.name: WO3 Nanoparticle Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Precipitating a H2WO4 gel by addition of concentrated HCl to aqueous Na2WO4. After several washings of H2WO4 carried out by redispersion/centrifugation, a stable H2WO4 sol was generated by peptization with oxalic acid at 60°C. The resulting colloidal suspension (having an overall mass of 8 to 8.5g in the typical preparation) was densified by adding 20% (w/w) Carbowax and a few drops of Triton X-100.
nodes.source_text: The preparation of colloidal WO3 was first accomplished by precipitating a H2WO4 gel by addition of concentrated HCl to aqueous Na2WO4... densified by adding 20% (w/w) Carbowax

nodes.name: FTO/WO3 Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Dry nanoparticulate films (colloidal photoanodes) were obtained onto the well-cleaned FTO glass by spin coating the H2WO4 aqueous colloidal precursor. Six WO3 layers were sequentially deposited, each layer being thermally annealed at 550°C for 30 min in air before the deposition of the next one.
nodes.source_text: Dry nanoparticulate films... six WO3 layers were sequentially deposited, each layer being thermally annealed at 550°C for 30 min in air

nodes.name: BiVO4 Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: 10 mM Bi(NO3)3 was slowly added to an acidic solution of 10 mM VOSO4. Dropwise addition of concentrated HNO3 over a 30 min period was necessary to achieve the complete dissolution of Bi(NO3)3. After this point, the pH was rapidly increased to 4.5 using 2 M CH3COONa. The resulting solution was quickly used as an electrolyte for two-electrode potentiostatic electrodeposition by applying 210 mV between FTO/WO3 and a platinum foil at room temperature for 300 s. The typical distance between the FTO/WO3 working electrode and the Pt foil was ≈3 mm. After deposition, the resulting FTO-supported photoanode was abundantly rinsed with water, dried at room temperature, and lastly annealed at 500°C in air for 2 hours.

nodes.name: CoFeOx Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: This catalyst was deposited by chronoamperometry at 1.2 V versus saturated calomel electrode (SCE) for either 30 s (1 nm thickness) or 300 s (10 nm thickness) under simulated AM 1.5G illumination on WO3/BiVO4 photoanodes. Reference FTO/CoFeOx was prepared with the same procedure, in absence of simulated sunlight.
nodes.source_text: Deposition of the CoFeOx catalyst was performed according to Liardet et al... for either 30 or 300 s under simulated AM 1.5G illumination

nodes.description: PEC OER performance - LSV under chopped AM 1.5G illumination
nodes.source_text: Figure 1A reports the linear sweep voltammetry under chopped AM 1.5G illumination... The PEC performance is remarkably improved by the addition of a thin CoFeOx layer (1 nm@BVO), as shown by a ≈400mV cathodic shift of the onset potential and a ≈20% increase of the saturation photocurrent. The incident photon-to-current conversion efficiency (IPCE) shown in fig. S4A shows that the highest quantum yield (ca. 40%) is achieved with the 1nm@BVO photoanode

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of CoFeO_x cocatalysts: dry 1nm@BVO shows Co^{2.0}, 10nm@BVO shows Co^{2.3}, 10nm@FTO ~Co^{3.0}; all stabilize to ~Co^{3.0} at OCP in electrolyte (pH 9).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3B displays the corresponding Co oxidation state determined from the absorption edge energy... dry 1nm@BVO and 10nm@BVO exhibits... Co^{+2.0} and Co^{+2.3}, respectively... Upon exposure to the electrolyte at OCP... stabilizes to approximately Co^{+3.0}.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS fitting of first Co-O shell: 1nm@BVO r_Co-O shrinks 2.03→1.88 Å, 10nm@BVO 1.92→1.88 Å upon electrolyte exposure at OCP; 10nm@FTO stable ~1.90 Å, consistent with CoOOH reference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co-O interatomic distance r_{Co-O} determined from EXAFS analysis (Fig. 3C)... strong shrinking (2.03→1.88Å) in 1nm@BVO, a milder one (1.92→1.88Å) in 10nm@BVO... value at OCP for 10nm@FTO agrees with r_{Co-O} = 1.902Å measured in CoOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando XANES shows potential-dependent Co oxidation state variations in dark and light; 10nm@FTO oxidizes above +1.1 V_RHE, 1nm@BVO reduces below +0.5 V_RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4 reports the oxidation state determined from XANES spectra recorded at different potentials... both in the dark and under AM 1.5G irradiation...

nodes.characterization_summary: FEXRAV reveals Co-specific redox processes: 10nm@FTO shows Co^{II/III} at E_eq = +1.33 V_RHE; 10nm@BVO shows two processes with E_eq = +1.5 V_RHE and interface-specific reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FEXRAV analysis enables precise correlation between the (photo)electrochemical activity and the redox behavior of the cocatalyst... The FEXRAV waves match quite well those observed in CVs...

nodes.characterization_summary: P-EIS shows surface state capacitance C_SS associated with CoFeO_x cocatalyst has bell-shaped distribution peaking 0.8-0.9 V_RHE, height correlates with cocatalyst thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The analysis of P-EIS data show that the capacitance associated with the cocatalyst has a bell-shaped distribution... C_SS is peaked around 0.8 to 0.9 V and spans the 0.6 to 1.0 V interval.
